region.text: 'the whole region of Sabah' under the Brunei grant, without the strips Brunei ceded in 1884-1885

ledger.note: 1877: Overbeck acquires the North Borneo grant from Brunei. 'The treaty was signed on 29 December 1877 at the Brunei Palace' by Sultan Abdul Momin, giving Overbeck 'the right over the whole region of Sabah', including Sandakan and Tawau. The British North Borneo page adds the 'concessions of the Sultanates of Brunei and Sulu in 1877 and 1878'.

region.text: the east coast of Sabah under the Sulu concession

ledger.note: 1878: the Sulu concession. 'This concession was signed on 22 January 1878 in the palace of the Sultan of Sulu', a concession in perpetuity negotiated for Dent's company by William Cowie. The extent is not on the page; the east coast is the researcher's reading.

1881: the Chartered Company. The British government granted a royal charter on 1 November 1881 (the Provisional Association was formed on 26 August 1881) and the British North Borneo Chartered Company took over.
1884: the capital moves from Kudat to Sandakan (photo caption: 'capital of North Borneo from 1884 to 1945').

region.text: the Putatan River, added from Brunei in May 1884

ledger.note: 1884: the Putatan River. The page lists 'the Putatan River (May 1884)' among the territory added from Brunei.

region.text: the Padas district, added from Brunei in November 1884 (centre at Beaufort, the researcher's coordinates)

ledger.note: 1884: the Padas district. The page lists 'the Padas district (November 1884)'. The Padas circle is the researcher's reading of the district.

region.text: the Kawang River, added from Brunei in February 1885 (centre at Papar, the researcher's coordinates)

ledger.note: 1885: the Kawang River, listed among the Brunei cessions as February 1885.

region.text: the Mantanani Islands and the Kota Belud coast opposite, added from Brunei in April 1885 (the researcher's coordinates)

ledger.note: 1885: the Mantanani Islands, listed among the Brunei cessions as April 1885. The Madrid Protocol of the same year (page: 'an agreement known as the Madrid Protocol was signed in Madrid') concerned Spanish claims.
1888: protectorate. 'North Borneo was made a British Protectorate on 12 May 1888.' The Company stays the administrator.

1890: the Company administers Labuan. 'In 1890, the Crown Colony of Labuan was incorporated into the administration of North Borneo.' [Reviewer se-03-x, 2026-10-24: counterpart was british-colonial-empire; colony-of-labuan carries the 1890 loss to this dossier]

region.text: minor Padas territories added in March 1898

ledger.note: 1898: further minor Padas territories from Brunei (the page's list gives March 1898 and no name); inside the Padas circle, so the shape does not change.

1904: Labuan returns to direct British rule: 'before returning to direct British rule in 1904'. [Reviewer se-03-x, 2026-10-24: counterpart was british-colonial-empire; colony-of-labuan carries the 1904 gain from this dossier]

region.text: the whole of Sabah, from Kudat and the west coast to Sandakan and Tawau

ledger.note: 1942: Japan takes North Borneo. 'Jesselton was occupied by the Japanese on 8 January' (Japanese forces had landed on Labuan on 3 January 1942); the territory was 'completely occupied' by the end of January.

region.text: the whole of Sabah, from Kudat and the west coast to Sandakan and Tawau

ledger.note: 1945: occupation ends. The war 'ended on 15 August 1945' (British North Borneo page) and the British Military Administration began in September; 'The official surrender took place in Labuan on 10 September 1945' (History of Sabah page).
1946: the capital moves to the Jesselton area ('the capital of North Borneo moved to the area in 1946').
1946: the Company hands over. The administration of the protectorate was ceded 'to the crown colony government on 15 July 1946'; the infobox: 'North Borneo ceded to the Crown Colony: 15 July 1946'.
1946: Labuan joins. 'The Crown Colony of Labuan joined the new Crown colony during its formation' (infobox: 15 July 1946).

region.text: the Turtle Islands and the Mangsee Islands, passed to the Philippine government (the researcher's approximate coordinates; the pages give none)

ledger.note: 1947: the Turtle and Mangsee Islands go to the Philippines. On 16 October 1947 'administration of the Turtle Islands and the Mangsee Islands' passed to the Philippine government; the History of Sabah page dates it to 1946 without a month. The islands' position is the researcher's.

region.text: Sabah, with Labuan as part until 1984

ledger.note: 1963: North Borneo becomes Sabah. Self-government on 31 August 1963; 'Malaysia Agreement: 16 September 1963'; 'It was succeeded as the state of Sabah through the formation of the Federation of Malaysia on 16 September 1963.'

wars.outcome: Japan landed on Labuan on 3 January 1942 and took Jesselton on 8 January; North Borneo was 'completely occupied' by the end of January 1942; the war ended on 15 August 1945 and the Japanese surrender in Labuan took place on 10 September 1945.
wars.note: Source for the war is the British North Borneo page; the surrender date is the History of Sabah page's.

certainty.note: The pages opened give no boundary: the Dutch (Sibuku, Sebatik) convention dates of 1891 and 1915, Cowie Harbour and the Sarawak boundary at Lawas are silent; the Brunei strips are circles. The Philippine islands of 1947 are sharp as a transfer but approximate on the map.

notes:
Written 2026-10-20 by the se-03-x additions batch: a colony Cliopatria lacks. Three pages opened (budget 2-5 for a state with no Cliopatria shapes).
Life: 29 December 1877 (Brunei's grant to Overbeck) to 16 September 1963 (Malaysia). The Wikipedia article 'British North Borneo' runs 1881-1946 and the Crown Colony of North Borneo has its own article (1946-1963); the dossier keeps one colour for the territory and records the 1881 charter, the 1888 protectorate and the 1946 Crown colony as rename events (rule 2). The BNB Company's first land is dated from the grants, not from the charter.
Unsettled: (1) The History of Sabah page says the 1877 grant covered 'the whole region of Sabah' but the British North Borneo page lists Brunei cessions of Putatan (May 1884), Padas (November 1884), Kawang (February 1885) and Mantanani (April 1885); the four strips are circles at the researcher's coordinates (Beaufort, Papar, Mantanani and the Putatan at Kota Kinabalu), not named on the pages. (2) The Sulu concession's extent is not on the page; the east coast is a reading. (3) The Sibuku and Sebatik Dutch boundary (1891, 1915), Tawau and Cowie Harbour, the Sulu confirmation of 1903 and the Philippine claim are all 'page silent' in the pages opened; the Spanish Madrid Protocol is only named. (4) The Turtle and Mangsee Islands (16 October 1947, Crown Colony page; 1946 on the History of Sabah page) have no gazetteer entries; the circle at 118.3E 6.0N is a drawing aid. (5) The Straits Settlements dossier dissolves on 1 April 1946 and sends Labuan to this colony (the Labuan page has the transfer on 15 July 1946); the Sarawak dossier names 'british-north-borneo-company' as the unconfirmed cedant of Lawas, and the Brunei dossier calls the same Company 'british-colonial-empire' in places. (6) Area: no page gives one (Sabah is 71,000 km2 in the gazetteer, so no comparison was possible). (7) Rulers: governors are not listed on the pages. (8) Gazetteer names needed: Turtle Islands (Taganak), Mangsee Islands, Papar, Beaufort, Kudat, Kota Belud, Mantanani, Sebatik.
